Daily Brief

The day's most consequential developments center on the unprecedented trilateral summit between Presidents Trump, Xi, and Putin in Shenzhen, with the three leaders meeting for the first time together ahead of Thursday's formal talks [BBC], [Nikkei Asia], [The Hindu]. The summit has drawn comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference, though officials are tempering expectations of immediate breakthroughs on Ukraine or Iran [Le Monde], [The Economist]. Meanwhile, tensions between the US and Iran escalated as Iran targeted American military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain following US strikes on Qeshm Island, raising fears of broader conflict [BBC], [Al Jazeera], [The Hindu]. In a significant blow to Russian logistics, Ukraine executed a multi-stage operation that collapsed a key span of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea [BBC], [Al Jazeera], [The Hindu]. On the technology front, Nvidia reported surging revenues of $116 billion while firmly rejecting ousted founder Jensen Huang's bid to return as CEO [BBC], [RNZ]. In US politics, Democrat Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska's Senate race completed a historic midterm sweep, giving Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority [France 24], [ABC Australia].

01 Geopolitics

Trump, Xi, and Putin Gather in Shenzhen for Historic Three-Way Summit

  • Trump arrived in Shenzhen where Xi Jinping greeted him on the tarmac; Trump later exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of Thursday's trilateral meeting
  • The three leaders will discuss Ukraine, Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions, and AI development; this marks the first time the US, Chinese, and Russian leaders have met together in person
  • Xi described China-Russia relations as 'a source of stability' in a 'turbulent world' during bilateral talks with Putin on Wednesday
  • Officials have downplayed expectations for substantive outcomes, describing the summit as more exploratory and symbolic

Ukraine Executes Multi-Stage Operation to Collapse Key Span of Crimean Bridge

  • A weeks-long Ukrainian operation systematically destroyed Russian air defenses before launching coordinated drone and missile strikes that collapsed a road bridge arch
  • President Zelenskyy confirmed Ukrainian-made Neptune and Flamingo missiles along with heavy drones were used in the 'unprecedented operation'
  • Road traffic is suspended and rail services restricted to one track; approximately 200 meters of roadway was heavily damaged and submerged
  • Russia's Kremlin spokesman said the bridge 'will be rebuilt' but analysts note Crimea is 'logistically turning into an island'

Nvidia Reports Doubled Revenue to $116 Billion, Rules Out Huang's Return as CEO

  • Nvidia reported quarterly sales of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, with profits doubling to $65 billion
  • Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors 'we've got this' in the company's first results since founder Jensen Huang's departure
  • Board chair Harvey Jones firmly rejected Huang's public statement that he would be 'honoured' to return, saying the board 'does not intend to reinstate him'
  • The company forecast revenue of $130 billion next quarter despite assuming no data-center chip sales to China

05 Policy

Democrat Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Race, Completing Historic Midterm Sweep

  • Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan with slightly over 50% of the vote after two weeks of ballot counting
  • The victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority after flipping nine GOP-held seats, their best midterm performance since 1958
  • Democrats also won Senate races in conservative states including South Carolina, Texas, Kansas, and Mississippi
  • Peltola overcame allegations that her campaign helped recruit an independent candidate sharing the Republican incumbent's name
